response.answer: NOTE: The Rome "Rene" 2027 is a brand-new model for the 2026/27 season. It replaces the "Rene-Gade" (which ran from the 2023/24 to 2025/26 seasons). Since the Rene 2027 is on preorder and not yet available for on-snow testing, reviews below are for the predecessor Rene-Gade, which shares lineage, rider association, and many design elements. Differences between the Rene 2027 and predecessor are noted where applicable. 1. brand: Rome (Rome SDS / Rome Snowboards) [1][2] 2. model_name: Rene [1] 3. model_year: 2027 (2026/27 season) [1] 4. predecessor_model_name: Rome Rene-Gade (also called "Renegade"), produced 2024–2026 seasons [3][4] 5. product_type: Snowboard [1] 6. board_category: All-Mountain / Freestyle [1][5] 7. gender: Men's [1][5] 8. pro_rider_name: Rene Rinnekangas (Finnish snowboarder, born 25 September 1999) [6][7] 9. pro rider nationality: Finnish, from Iisalmi, Finland [7] 10. pro rider competitive credentials: 2018 Winter Olympian, 2019 Winter X Games slopestyle silver medallist, 2026 Milano Cortina Olympic participant [7][8] 11. design philosophy: The Rene 2027 is "a new addition to the lineup, stepping in as the replacement for the Renegade and built around how Rene Rinnekangas actually rides" [3] 12. model series: Rome Signature Collection [9] 13. model_first_available_year: 2024 (2023/24 season); it "replaced the National" in the Rome lineup [10][11] 14. model_first_available_year: 2026/27 season — currently on preorder, estimated delivery May 2026 [1] 15. manufacturer: Rome Snowboards (Rome SDS) [12] 16. manufacturer founding year: 2001 [12][13] 17. manufacturer founders: Josh Reed and Paul Maravetz [13] 18. manufacturer headquarters: Waterbury, Vermont, USA [12][13] 19. manufacturer ethos: "All Ways Down" — freestyle-oriented, rider-driven design [13] 20. brand director (2026/27 season): Ben Morse [14] 21. price_aud_merchant: $949.99 AUD — preorder [1] 22. price_aud_merchant: $949.99 AUD [1] 23. price_aud_merchant: $949.99 AUD [1] 24. availability_status: Preorder, estimated May 2026 delivery [1] 25. availability_status: Listed for sale at snowcentral.com.au [15] 26. Rene-Gade EUR price at SnowCountry: €449.96 [20] 37. shape: Directional Twin [1][3] 38. shape description (merchant): Slightly longer nose than tail, balanced for freestyle riding with more drive when riding forward [3] 39. camber_type: Fusion Camber [1][3] 40. camber_description: "Positive camber between the bindings with rocker in the nose and tail" — strong edge hold and pop while keeping tips smoother and more forgiving [3] DISAGREEMENT — Camber Type: The predecessor Rene-Gade used "Stay Positive Camber" (full traditional camber) [21][22]. The new Rene 2027 uses "Fusion Camber" (hybrid positive camber with rocker pockets at contact points) [1][3]. This is a significant design change. The new Rene is more forgiving at the tips than the predecessor. 41. camber_type: Stay Positive Camber — full traditional camber with no rocker [21][22] 42. 3D shape: Directional Diamond 3D ("wide flat section in middle, 3D curve tapering past contact points in nose") [1] 43. tail design: Tail Double Kick ("aggressive two-part rise in tail for more pop, enhanced torsional stability, smoother landings") [1] 44. sidecut_type: Radial Sidecut (single radius) [1][22] 45. taper: 0cm (zero taper across all sizes per Ballistyx size chart) [3] 46. setback: 0cm (zero setback across all sizes per Ballistyx size chart) [3] 47. flex_rating_10: 7/10 (mid-stiff) [1][3] DISAGREEMENT — Flex Rating: The predecessor Rene-Gade was rated at flex 8/10 by Rome's own 2024 spec [23], 9/10 by SkatePro and Ski Pro AZ for the 2026 model [24][25], and described as "the stiffest of all Rome's go-anywhere boards" by Whitelines [19]. The new Rene 2027 at 7/10 represents a softer flex than the predecessor, consistent with the shift from full camber to Fusion Camber for broader accessibility. 48. flex_rating_10_manufacturer: 8/10 [23] 49. flex_rating_10: 9/10 [24] 50. flex_feel: "A responsive medium-stiff flex that adds stability and power compared to softer freestyle boards" [3] 51. core_material: Pop Core — "alternating 20mm wide Poplar and Paulownia wood strips" [1][3] DISAGREEMENT — Core Type: The Rene 2027 uses "Pop Core" (20mm/20mm poplar/paulownia strips). The predecessor Rene-Gade used "SuperPop Core" (10mm poplar / 20mm paulownia strips — "lightest and most responsive core") [26][27]. The Rome tech page defines Pop Core as "most versatile and durable" vs SuperPop as "lightest and most responsive" [28]. This is a construction change. 52. core_material: SuperPop Core (alternating 10mm poplar / 20mm paulownia strips) [26][27] 53. laminate: Triax Glass upper and lower (triaxial fiberglass running in three different angles) [1][3] 54. laminate: "Fiberglass running in three different axes, built for torsional rigidity and added snap" [28] 55. construction_material_innovation: Directional Triple Bamboo Omega HotRods [1][3] 56. construction_material_innovation: Bamboo HotRods in a directional triple configuration with Omega carbon sleeves — "add a layered, progressive snap through the board, giving it a deeper, more loaded response" [3] DISAGREEMENT — HotRod Material: The predecessor Rene-Gade used "Directional Triple Carbon Omega HotRods" (carbon rods with carbon Omega wrappers) [21][22]. The Rene 2027 uses "Directional Triple Bamboo Omega HotRods" (bamboo rods with Omega wrappers) [1][3]. Rome's official tech page describes bamboo HotRods as "pressable and playful with plenty of pop" vs carbon HotRods as "super responsive and powerfully snappy" [28]. This is another significant change toward a more playful feel. 57. construction_material_innovation: Directional Triple Carbon Omega HotRods [21][22] 58. base_material: SinterStrong Base — "low maintenance sintered, versatile and fast" [1][3] DISAGREEMENT — Base Material: The predecessor Rene-Gade used "SinterSpeed Base" — Rome's "fastest sintered base, built for maximum speed and performance" [21][22]. The Rene 2027 uses "SinterStrong Base" — described as "versatile, low-maintenance" [1][3][28]. SinterSpeed is the premium tier; SinterStrong is a step below. This may affect top-end glide performance. 59. base_material: SinterSpeed Base ("Rome's fastest sintered base") [21][22] 60. sidewall_material: Not explicitly stated for the Rene 2027.
